meta.spec_reference: Standard MIDI Files 1.0 (MIDI Manufacturers Association, RP-001, 1996 revision of the 1988 specification) for the chunk structure, variable-length quantities, track events and meta-events; MIDI 1.0 Detailed Specification v4.2 (MMA, 1996) for status bytes, the 0-127 data-byte range, running status, channel voice messages, Channel Mode messages (controllers 120-127) and System Exclusive framing; General MIDI System Level 1 (MMA MP-002) for the program-number and key-number conventions.

schema_extensions.name: dotted keys for fields inside anonymous nested structs
schema_extensions.where: the MidiMessage.note_off_event.*, note_on_event.*, note_pressure_event.*, controller_event.*, program_event.*, channel_pressure_event.*, pitch_bend_event.*, meta_event.* and sysex_event.* entries
schema_extensions.why: The schema keys entries as STRUCT_TYPENAME.field_name, but every event body in this template is an anonymous struct with only an instance name - `struct { ... } note_off_event;` at line 79, `struct { ... } meta_event;` at line 234, and seven more. There is no typename to use, and several field names are reused across sibling branches (m_note appears at lines 77, 85 and 93; m_velocity at 78 and 86; m_pressure at 94 and 116; m_length at 152 and 240), so a single-level key would collide. A two-level dotted key names the enclosing typedef'd struct, then the anonymous instance, then the field; every component is a literal identifier from the .bt, so nothing is invented.

schema_extensions.name: fixed_result / fixed_result_hex
schema_extensions.why: The header length is both a byte count AND an invariant, because the header chunk data is three fixed-size fields. fixed_result records the constant 6 so the rewrite step can emit it directly, while algorithm/covers/includes_self still document what it measures.

schema_extensions.name: lookahead sub-keys: values_hex, comparison, mask, read_then_unread_line
schema_extensions.why: The status byte is not decided by a peek in the ordinary sense - it is READ into a field and then conditionally UN-READ by FSeek(FTell()-1) at line 70 when bit 7 is clear, so that the same byte is re-consumed as running-status data. read_then_unread_line records that. The nine dispatch comparisons are also masked rather than exact (`(lastStatus & 0xf0) == 0x80` and so on), so `comparison` and `mask` record that the mined value set is a set of high nibbles with a free channel nibble beneath, not a set of whole-byte literals - without which a generator would emit only channel 0.

schema_extensions.name: template_deviations
schema_extensions.why: This template is the laxest of the set: it contains not one Assert, Warning or Exit, and it never compares either magic number against anything. Beyond that it disagrees with the specification in fourteen concrete places - signed `char` for every unsigned data byte, signed `short` for the track count and the division word, an ignored header length, a 24-bit bitfield compensated with an FSeek, a variable-length guard that silently truncates a five-byte quantity, a running-status variable never reset between tracks, and an event-loop counter that wraps to 2^32 on overshoot and hangs. A generator that imitated the parser's laxity would emit files this template accepts and no sequencer does, so these must be visible as data rather than buried in prose.

schema_extensions.name: generation_range on a field the schema would call free-form
schema_extensions.where: MidiMessage.m_dtime, and the per-note key-number entries
schema_extensions.why: Delta time is nominally a free musical value, but it is the one number in the format that multiplies with the tick division to decide when an event actually sounds, and its encodable maximum of 0x0FFFFFFF ticks schedules an event days into the future. Likewise a key number is spec-legal across 0-127 but silent outside roughly 36-96 on a General MIDI instrument. Recording practical bounds on these keeps generated files musically reachable rather than merely parseable.

meta.structure_note: A chunk stream with no terminator: a fixed 14-byte 'MThd' header declaring the format, the track count and the tick division, followed by exactly that many 'MTrk' chunks, each a 4-byte type, a 32-bit big-endian byte count, and an event stream of variable-length delta times and status-dispatched events that must end with the mandatory End of Track meta-event inside the counted region.

MidiHeader.m_magic.description: The four-character chunk type that opens every Standard MIDI File; a file that does not begin with it is not a MIDI file.
MidiHeader.m_magic.notes: The template's own header records this at line 11 as `//  ID Bytes: 4D 54 68 64 //MThd`, but the struct performs no Assert and no comparison of any kind - it simply reads four bytes. SMF 1.0 (MIDI 1.0 Detailed Specification, RP-001): 'MThd' is the header chunk type and must be the first four bytes of the file. This is the single most important fixed value in the format and must never receive an evil value.

MidiHeader.m_seclen.description: Byte count of the header chunk data following this length field; the header data is three 16-bit fields, so the value is invariably 6.
MidiHeader.m_seclen.covers: the three header data fields that follow it - m_format, m_ntracks and m_tickdiv, two bytes each; it excludes the four magic bytes and this length field itself

generation_range.rationale: A 32-bit length that the template reads and then completely ignores - it reads the three header fields by shape, not by length. A conforming reader instead skips exactly m_seclen bytes, so any value other than 6 leaves it positioned in the wrong place for the first MTrk chunk. Uniform generation would also claim up to 4 GB of header.

MidiHeader.m_seclen.notes: SMF 1.0: 'MThd <length> <format> <ntrks> <division>' where <length> is a 32-bit value giving the number of bytes in the chunk data, always 6 for a header chunk. The specification permits a longer header for future expansion, requiring readers to skip the excess, but no encoder writes one.

MidiHeader.m_format.description: The overall organisation of the file: a single multi-channel track, several simultaneous tracks, or several independent patterns.
value_names: MIDI_MULTIPLE - one or more simultaneous tracks of a single sequence
MIDI_PATTERN - one or more sequentially independent single-track patterns
MidiHeader.m_format.notes: Anonymous enum at lines 24-29. SMF 1.0 defines exactly these three formats and states that readers should reject a format they do not recognise. Format 1 is preferred for generation: it is the form nearly every sequencer writes and reads, and unlike format 0 it does not pin the track count to 1.

MidiHeader.m_ntracks.description: Number of MTrk chunks that follow the header; it is the array bound for the track list, so it must equal the number of track chunks actually present.
MidiHeader.m_ntracks.covers: the MidiTrack tracks[] array that follows the header chunk; it excludes the header chunk itself

generation_range.rationale: Used directly as the array bound at line 260 with no check. Each track is a full MTrk chunk with its own event stream, so this count directly multiplies file size; and because the template reads exactly this many chunks, a value larger than the number of chunks actually written drives the parse off the end of the file. 1-4 tracks exercises the multi-track path while keeping files small.

MidiHeader.m_ntracks.notes: SMF 1.0: '<ntrks> is a 16-bit value specifying the number of track chunks in the file'. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: declared as `short`, which is SIGNED in 010 Editor, so a track count above 32767 reads as negative and the array bound becomes negative. The specification's field is unsigned, 0-65535, though a file with zero tracks carries no music and format 0 pins the value to 1.

MidiHeader.m_tickdiv.description: Time division: bit 15 selects between metrical time (ticks per quarter note) and timecode (SMPTE frames), and the remaining bits mean entirely different things in the two modes.
MidiHeader.m_tickdiv.valid_bits: bit 15 is the mode flag. When it is 0 the whole 15-bit remainder (bits 14-0) is ticks per quarter note, 1-32767. When it is 1 the field is two signed bytes: bits 15-8 are a negative SMPTE frame rate, restricted to -24, -25, -29 (30 drop-frame) or -30, and bits 7-0 are ticks per frame, 1-255. No other bit pattern is meaningful.

generation_range.rationale: Metrical mode only. The tick resolution is the denominator of every delta time in the file, so an extreme value makes every event time meaningless without adding coverage; and a value of 0 in metrical mode is a division by zero in any player computing seconds per tick. 24-960 spans every resolution real sequencers use.

MidiHeader.m_tickdiv.notes: SMF 1.0: '<division> ... If bit 15 of <division> is a zero, the bits 14 thru 0 represent the number of delta-time ticks which make up a quarter-note. If bit 15 of <division> is a one, delta-times in a file correspond to subdivisions of a second, in a way consistent with SMPTE and MIDI time code.' TEMPLATE DEVIATION: declared as `short`, which is signed, so every timecode-mode value (bit 15 set) reads as a negative number. The template performs no check of any kind on this field.

DeltaTime.t0.description: Byte 1 of a variable-length quantity; bit 7 is the continuation flag saying whether another byte follows, and the low seven bits carry that byte's slice of the value.
DeltaTime.t0.valid_bits: 0x7F carries the value; bit 0x80 is the continuation flag - set means t1 follows, clear means this is the last byte
value_names: continuation bit clear - this is the final byte of the quantity
DeltaTime.t0.notes: SMF 1.0, 'Variable-length quantities': 'numbers are represented in 7 bits per byte, most significant bits first. All bytes except the last have bit 7 set, and the last byte has bit 7 clear. If the number is between 0 and 127, it is thus represented exactly as one byte.' The maximum is four bytes, giving 0x0FFFFFFF. The template accumulates the value into the local `total` at lines 36-58 by shifting left 7 and adding the low seven bits of each byte. valid_values records the two legal states of the masked continuation bit, not of the whole byte. Canonical encoders emit no redundant leading zero groups, so a multi-byte quantity should never begin with the byte 0x80. The template declares every MIDI data byte as `char`, which is SIGNED in 010 Editor, so any byte with bit 7 set reads as negative. That is why the meta-event test at line 127 is `lastStatus == -1` rather than `== 0xFF`. A generator must treat these fields as unsigned 8-bit values.

MidiMessage.m_dtime.description: Variable-length delta time: the number of ticks between the previous event in this track and this one; every event in every track carries one.
MidiMessage.m_dtime.algorithm: variable-length quantity, big-endian septets: value = sum over the 1 to 4 bytes of (byte & 0x7F) shifted left by 7 for each byte that follows it; every byte but the last has bit 7 set
MidiMessage.m_dtime.covers: the 1 to 4 bytes preceding this event's status byte; it excludes the status byte and all event data

generation_range.rationale: The encodable maximum is 0x0FFFFFFF ticks. With a typical division of 480 ticks per quarter note that is over 155000 quarter notes for a single gap, which makes a player schedule an event days into the future. 0-1920 keeps every gap within four quarter notes at 480 ticks and, just as importantly, keeps the VLQ to one or two bytes so the encoding stays canonical.

MidiMessage.m_dtime.notes: SMF 1.0: '<MTrk event> = <delta-time><event>' and 'delta-time is stored as a variable-length quantity. It represents the amount of time before the following event.' The first event of a track is conventionally at delta time 0. The value is a DELTA, not an absolute time, so it can never be negative and needs no reference point.

MidiMessage.m_status.description: The event status byte: bit 7 distinguishes a real status byte from a running-status data byte, bits 6-4 select the message type and bits 3-0 carry the MIDI channel.
MidiMessage.m_status.valid_bits: bit 7 must be SET for this byte to be a status byte at all; if it is clear the byte is the first data byte of a running-status message and the template un-reads it. For 0x80-0xEF bits 6-4 are the message type and bits 3-0 are the channel, 0-15, which are free. For 0xF0-0xFF the whole byte is a system message code and there is no channel nibble.

MidiMessage.meta_event.m_type.description: The meta-event type byte following the 0xFF status; it names what the event carries and fixes the shape and often the exact length of the data that follows.
MidiMessage.meta_event.m_type.notes: Anonymous enum at lines 131-151, dispatched on by the if/else chain at lines 153-233. SMF 1.0 requires every meta-event type byte to be in 0x00-0x7F, so bit 7 must be clear; the specification also instructs readers to skip an unrecognised type using its length field, which is what the template's final else at line 230 does. META_END_OF_TRACK (0x2F) is preferred because it is mandatory in every track, so a generator must be able to emit it. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: the enum's base type is `char`, which is signed, so a type byte with bit 7 set would read negative and match no case. The track terminator is this format's one block terminator and it is a (type, length) PAIR rather than a single field: the exact bytes are FF 2F 00 - the 0xFF meta status, this type byte 0x2F, and a zero length - preceded by its delta time, so a minimal legal track is the four bytes 00 FF 2F 00. Because the terminator spans three fields it cannot be recorded as one fixed_value entry; the type is pinned here as the preferred_value, the length is pinned to 0 by a dependency, and the position is pinned by a last_element rule in the structure section.

structure.subject: MidiHeader
structure.detail: the four bytes 'MThd' must occupy file offsets 0-3, followed by the 32-bit length 6 and the six header bytes; nothing may precede them
structure.description: Every Standard MIDI File begins with the MThd header chunk, which is what identifies the file at all.
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed 14-byte head element - 'MThd', the constant length 6, then format, track count and division - with no randomisation of the magic and no evil-bit substitution

structure.subject: MidiTrack
structure.detail: at least one MTrk chunk must follow the header; a file with no track chunk carries no music
structure.description: The track chunk is the only place events live, so a file without one is empty.
structure.generation_note: emit at least one MTrk after the header and set MidiHeader.m_ntracks from the number actually written

structure.subject: file.tracks
structure.detail: exactly MidiHeader.m_ntracks track chunks, no more and no fewer; the template reads precisely that many with no end-of-file guard
structure.description: The header's track count is the only thing that tells a reader how many chunks to expect.
structure.generation_bound: 1 to 4 tracks, each event stream capped at 4 KB, holding generated files under roughly 16 KB. The count multiplies file size directly and a count larger than the chunks written drives the parse off the end of the file.
structure.generation_note: generate the tracks first as a bounded array, then set m_ntracks from the array length - never choose the two independently

structure.subject: MidiHeader then file.tracks
structure.detail: the header chunk comes first and every track chunk follows it, back to back with no gaps and no padding between chunks
structure.description: MIDI chunks are located purely by position and length, so any gap desynchronises everything after it.
structure.generation_note: emit the header as a fixed head element, then the track array, and write nothing between chunks

structure.subject: MidiTrack.m_magic, MidiTrack.m_seclen, the event stream
structure.detail: a track chunk is the four bytes 'MTrk', a 32-bit length, and then exactly that many bytes of events, with nothing interleaved
structure.description: The chunk envelope is what makes the file self-delimiting; the event stream has no terminator of its own beyond the counted End of Track event.
structure.generation_bound: one envelope per track, at most 4 tracks
structure.generation_note: generate the event stream first, measure it, then write the magic and the measured length - the length can never be chosen before the events exist

structure.subject: MidiMessage.meta_event with m_type META_END_OF_TRACK
structure.detail: the final event of every track chunk must be the End of Track meta-event, encoded as the three bytes FF 2F 00 preceded by its delta time, and it must lie inside the region m_seclen counts
structure.description: SMF 1.0 states the End of Track event is not optional; it is what gives a track an exact ending point.
structure.generation_bound: exactly one per track, always last
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed tail element of every track's bounded event array; a minimal legal track is the four bytes 00 FF 2F 00

structure.subject: MidiMessage within a track
structure.detail: the event loop is `while (remaining)`, an unbounded walk driven purely by the track length field with no event-count limit of any kind
structure.description: The body of a track is an unbounded repetition of events, which a generator must bound explicitly.
structure.generation_bound: 8 to 64 events per track, with meta and SysEx payloads capped at 64 bytes and delta times at 1920 ticks, holding each track's event stream under about 4 KB. This loop is the format's principal size lever, and it is also its principal hang risk: `remaining` is a local uint decremented by sizeof(message), so an overshoot wraps towards 2^32.
structure.generation_note: replace the while loop with a bounded array of event elements followed by a fixed End of Track event, then set m_seclen from the measured total

structure.subject: MidiMessage.m_dtime
structure.detail: every event in every track, without exception, is preceded by a variable-length delta time - including the End of Track event
structure.description: The delta time is not optional or omissible the way a running-status byte is; it is always present.
structure.generation_bound: one per event, 1 to 4 bytes each
structure.generation_note: always emit the delta time first, even when it is zero, which encodes as the single byte 0x00

structure.subject: DeltaTime
structure.detail: a variable-length quantity is 1 to 4 bytes: every byte but the last has bit 7 set, and the last has bit 7 clear
structure.description: The variable-length encoding is self-delimiting through its continuation bits and is capped at four bytes, giving a maximum of 0x0FFFFFFF.
structure.generation_bound: 1 to 2 bytes, i.e. values 0-16383. Longer quantities encode delta times and lengths so large that the file becomes either enormous or musically meaningless, and the 4-byte form is the one the template's own missing fifth-byte guard mishandles.
structure.generation_note: generate the numeric value first, bounded, then encode it canonically with no redundant leading zero groups - a multi-byte quantity must never begin with the byte 0x80

structure.subject: MidiMessage.m_status on the first event of a track
structure.detail: the first event of a track must carry an explicit status byte, because running status has nothing to inherit from
structure.description: SMF 1.0 requires running status to be reset at the start of every track, so an opening running-status byte is undefined.
structure.generation_bound: one explicit status byte at minimum per track
structure.generation_note: always emit an explicit status byte on the first event; the template's local lastStatus starts at 0 and is never reset between tracks, so an opening running-status message would match no dispatch branch, consume no data bytes and spin the event loop

structure.subject: running status after a meta or SysEx event
structure.detail: a System Exclusive or meta event cancels running status, so the next event must carry an explicit status byte
structure.description: SMF 1.0: 'Sysex events and meta events cancel any running status which was in effect.'
structure.generation_bound: not applicable - this is an exclusion, not a repeating element
structure.generation_note: emit an explicit status byte on any event that follows a meta or SysEx event; the template never clears lastStatus, so it would silently reuse a stale channel status

structure.subject: MidiMessage.meta_event with m_type META_SEQUENCE_NUM
structure.detail: if present, the Sequence Number event must be the very first event of a track, before any non-zero delta time and before any transmittable MIDI event
structure.condition: only when a Sequence Number event is emitted at all
structure.description: SMF 1.0 pins this meta-event to the start of a track so a Cue event can identify the sequence.
structure.generation_note: if emitted, place it as the first element of the track's event array with a delta time of 0

structure.subject: MidiMessage.meta_event with m_type META_COPYRIGHT
structure.detail: if present, the Copyright Notice should be the first event of the first track, at time 0
structure.condition: only when a Copyright Notice event is emitted at all
structure.description: SMF 1.0 gives the copyright event a required position so it can be found without scanning the whole file.
structure.generation_note: if emitted, place it at the head of track 0's event array

structure.subject: tempo-map meta-events in a format 1 file
structure.detail: Set Tempo, Time Signature, Key Signature and SMPTE Offset must all live in the first track, which carries no channel voice events
structure.description: Format 1 defines track 0 as a tempo map shared by every other track.
structure.generation_bound: 0 or 1 of each per file, all in track 0
structure.generation_note: when generating format 1, route every timing meta-event into the first track element and every channel voice event into the others

structure.subject: metrical and timecode division modes
structure.detail: bit 15 of MidiHeader.m_tickdiv selects one interpretation of the field or the other; there is no mixed mode, and the choice changes what every delta time in the file means
structure.description: The division field is a tagged union of two entirely different encodings.
structure.generation_note: pick metrical mode (bit 15 clear, 24-960 ticks per quarter note) unless deliberately exercising the SMPTE path, and derive the delta-time generation bound from the resolution chosen

structure.subject: MidiMessage.sysex_event with status 0xF0
structure.detail: requires the final byte of m_message to be the 0xF7 terminator, and the length field counts that terminator
structure.description: A normal SysEx message is self-terminating; without the 0xF7 a receiver waits forever for the rest of the message.
structure.generation_note: generate the manufacturer ID and body as data bytes 0-127, append 0xF7, then set the length from the measured total

structure.subject: MIDI System Common and System Real Time status bytes

structure.description: These messages exist only on the wire; SMF defines no file encoding for them, and this template would read a length field that is not there.
structure.generation_bound: not applicable - this is an exclusion, not a repeating element
structure.generation_note: restrict generated status bytes to 0x80-0xEF, 0xF0, 0xF7 and 0xFF; the template routes every excluded value to sysex_event, which is its most destructive desynchronisation path

structure.subject: any bytes after the last track chunk
structure.detail: the file ends with the last MTrk chunk's final counted byte; SMF defines nothing after it
structure.description: The template reads exactly m_ntracks chunks and stops, so trailing bytes are simply outside the format.
structure.generation_note: stop writing immediately after the last track's End of Track event

structure.subject: the chunk envelope
structure.detail: every chunk in the file is a four-character type followed by a 32-bit big-endian byte count and then exactly that many bytes; readers must skip a chunk of an unknown type using its length
structure.description: The four-byte type plus length envelope is the invariant that makes the whole file self-delimiting and forward-compatible.
structure.generation_bound: one envelope per chunk, at most 5 chunks
structure.generation_note: generate each chunk's payload first, then write its type and measured length; BigEndian() is set at line 18 and never changed, so every multi-byte field in the file is big-endian

template_deviations.subject: every data byte declared as `char`
template_deviations.issue: The template declares m_status, every channel voice data byte, every meta-event scalar and the SysEx payload as `char`, which is SIGNED in 010 Editor. Any byte with bit 7 set therefore reads as negative, which is why the meta-event test at line 127 is `lastStatus == -1` rather than a comparison against 0xFF.
template_deviations.impact: A generator that respects the declared signed type would emit only half the byte range for the status byte and would treat the 0-127 data-byte constraint as -128..127. Every one of these fields is unsigned in the MIDI specification, and for the data bytes the true range is 0-127, not 0-255.
template_deviations.action: Treat all of them as unsigned 8-bit; constrain every channel voice data byte to 0-127 and the status byte to 0x80-0xFF.

template_deviations.subject: MidiHeader.m_ntracks and MidiHeader.m_tickdiv
template_deviations.issue: Both are declared `short`, which is signed, where SMF 1.0 defines them as 16-bit unsigned. For m_tickdiv this is worse than cosmetic: every timecode-mode value has bit 15 set and so reads as negative.
template_deviations.impact: A track count above 32767 becomes a negative array bound, and the entire SMPTE division mode is misrepresented.
template_deviations.action: Treat both as unsigned 16-bit; decode m_tickdiv by testing bit 15 rather than the sign.

template_deviations.subject: neither magic number is ever checked
template_deviations.issue: Neither MidiHeader.m_magic nor MidiTrack.m_magic is compared against anything - no Assert, no if, no Warning. The template simply reads four bytes and continues.
template_deviations.impact: The template will happily parse a file that is not a MIDI file at all, and its laxity here says nothing about validity. These are the two most important fixed values in the format.
template_deviations.action: Treat 'MThd' and 'MTrk' as hard fixed values that never receive an evil value.

template_deviations.subject: MidiHeader.m_seclen is read and ignored
template_deviations.issue: The header length is read into a field and then never used: the template reads m_format, m_ntracks and m_tickdiv by shape rather than skipping m_seclen bytes.
template_deviations.impact: A wrong header length is invisible to this template and fatal to a conforming reader, which would be left positioned in the wrong place for the first MTrk chunk.

template_deviations.subject: MidiTrack event loop counter underflow
template_deviations.issue: `local uint remaining = m_seclen;` at line 250 is decremented by `sizeof(message)` at line 253 inside `while (remaining)`. There is no check that the subtraction stays non-negative, and remaining is unsigned.
template_deviations.impact: If the events overshoot the declared track length by even one byte the counter wraps to a value near 2^32 and the loop runs essentially forever. This is not a mis-parse, it is a hang - the single most dangerous property of this template for a generator that chooses m_seclen independently of the events.
template_deviations.action: Always derive m_seclen from the events actually written; never draw it at random.

template_deviations.subject: DeltaTime accepts an over-long variable-length quantity
template_deviations.issue: The guard `if (!(t3 & 0x80)) break;` breaks when the fourth byte's continuation bit is CLEAR. When it is SET the struct falls off its end and no fifth byte is read.
template_deviations.impact: A five-byte variable-length quantity is silently truncated to four, and everything after it in the track is mis-parsed. The specification caps the quantity at four bytes, so t3's continuation bit must always be clear.
template_deviations.action: Always emit t3 with bit 7 clear; better still, keep generated quantities to one or two bytes.

template_deviations.subject: lastStatus is never reset between tracks
template_deviations.issue: `local char lastStatus = 0;` is declared once at file scope and updated at line 68, but never cleared at the start of a track nor after a meta or SysEx event. SMF 1.0 requires running status to be reset at the start of every track and cancelled by every SysEx and meta event.
template_deviations.impact: The template will happily decode a running-status message at the start of track 2 using a status left over from track 1. Worse, if the first event of track 1 uses running status, lastStatus is still 0, no dispatch branch matches, no data bytes are consumed, and the event loop spins on a zero-size message.
template_deviations.action: Always emit an explicit status byte on the first event of every track and on the first event after any meta or SysEx event.

template_deviations.subject: META_TEMPO 24-bit bitfield
template_deviations.issue: `uint m_usecPerQuarterNote : 24;` is a 24-bit bitfield of a uint, which in 010 Editor occupies the storage of a full uint - four bytes - so the template compensates with `FSeek(FTell() - 1);` at line 208 to give the fourth byte back.
template_deviations.impact: A generator reading the declared type literally would emit four bytes where the format has three, shifting every subsequent event in the track by one byte.
template_deviations.action: Emit exactly three big-endian bytes for the tempo value.

template_deviations.subject: META_SEQUENCER_EVENT has no dispatch branch
template_deviations.issue: The enum declares META_SEQUENCER_EVENT = 0x7f at line 150 but the if/else chain at lines 153-233 has no branch for it, so it falls into the final else and is read as opaque m_data.
template_deviations.impact: None for generation - the length-delimited fallback is exactly what SMF 1.0 requires of a reader that does not recognise a meta type. Recorded so the gap reads as a deliberate fallback rather than an oversight.
template_deviations.action: Generate it as a length-delimited opaque payload beginning with a manufacturer ID.

template_deviations.subject: System Common and System Real Time statuses fall into sysex_event
template_deviations.issue: The test `(lastStatus & 0xf0) == 0xF0` at line 236 catches 0xF0 through 0xFE (0xFF having been taken by the meta branch at line 127), so 0xF1-0xF6 and 0xF8-0xFE all reach the SysEx branch and have a variable-length length read for them.
template_deviations.impact: These messages carry no length field, so the template consumes following event bytes as a length and then as a payload, desynchronising the rest of the track.
template_deviations.action: Never emit a status byte outside 0x80-0xEF, 0xF0, 0xF7 and 0xFF.

template_deviations.subject: MidiMessage.meta_event.m_name declared twice
template_deviations.issue: The same field name is used for the Sequence/Track Name meta-event at line 167 and for the Instrument Name meta-event at line 171, in mutually exclusive branches of the same if/else chain.
template_deviations.impact: Only one of the two can exist in any given parse, so a single constraints entry covers both; recorded so the duplicate key is not read as a collision.
template_deviations.action: Treat as one field whose meaning depends on m_type.

template_deviations.subject: MidiMessage.meta_event.m_fps is a frame count, not a frame rate
template_deviations.issue: The field name suggests frames per second, but SMF 1.0's SMPTE Offset event places the frame NUMBER within the second here; the frame RATE is packed into bits 6-5 of the hour byte at line 212.
template_deviations.impact: A generator following the name would write 24, 25 or 30 as a rate where the format expects a frame index bounded by that rate.
template_deviations.action: Emit a frame index 0-29 here and encode the rate in the hour byte.

template_deviations.subject: no bounds check anywhere on a variable-length length
template_deviations.issue: m_length.total is used directly as an array size at lines 159, 163, 167, 171, 175, 179, 183, 187, 191, 232 and 241, with no check against the remaining track length or the file size.
template_deviations.impact: A four-byte variable-length quantity can claim 256 MB from four bytes of input, and nothing stops the array from running past the end of the chunk or the file.
template_deviations.action: Bound every generated length to the payload actually written and keep it inside the enclosing track length.

template_deviations.subject: no Assert, no Warning and no Exit anywhere in the file
template_deviations.issue: The template contains not a single validation guard. Every constraint recorded here with source 'spec' is one the parser does not check at all, and even the two magic numbers pass unexamined.
template_deviations.impact: The set of files this template accepts is very much larger than the set of valid MIDI files, so its behaviour is no guide to validity.
template_deviations.action: Take every 'spec'-sourced constraint in this file as binding despite the template's silence.
